summary: No cost target or quantity is stated; the design is a simple single part, with stock waste and 4 setups as the main cost drivers (rough estimate EUR 55-130 per part at batch 10).

flags.title: Buy-to-fly about 5-6 from a block; consider a nearer stock size or a plate plus upright
flags.evidence: snapshot parts[0].volume_mm3 = 62300 (0.168 kg). Bbox 125x60x40 = 300000 mm3, ratio 4.8. Realistic stock with machining allowance (about 130x65x45 = 380000 mm3, 1.0 kg) gives a ratio of about 6.1. Assumed 6082 at EUR 4-8/kg, so roughly EUR 4-8 of material, of which about 80% becomes chips. Material cost is small in absolute terms.
flags.recommendation: If the quantity is above about 10, check whether an extruded or standard-profile L or flat bar (for example 60x40 bar cut to 125) cuts the roughing time. Otherwise accept it: material is not the main driver.

suggested_change.detail: Choose stock: 130x65x45 block, or an L-profile or plate with a welded or bolted upright

flags.title: Single deep Ø3 side hole forces its own setup, tool and operation
flags.evidence: snapshot holes[1]: Ø3 x 36 mm blind along X (depth/Ø = 12), feature 'Pin hole', count 1. setup_directions includes -x only for this and the side faces. Hole purpose is not stated in the blueprint. Adds about 5-10 min of handling and drilling, with peck cycles and tool-break risk.
flags.recommendation: Confirm the pin hole is needed. If it is, shorten it, enlarge it (Ø4-5), or make it reachable from a setup already used (+z or -z).

suggested_change.detail: Justify or relocate the Ø3x36 pin hole; the blueprint has no requirement for it

flags.title: About 5 distinct tools for a small part
flags.evidence: snapshot: Ø8.4 through (x4), Ø15 counterbore (x4), Ø3 pin hole, pocket with 6 mm corner radius (D2@Pocket1 = 6), R2 fillets (internal_radii_mm, count 2). Each extra tool adds a change and offset check. R2 implies a Ø4 cutter, below the CON-003 Ø6 minimum (owned by DFM).
flags.recommendation: Use one corner radius of at least R3 for the pocket and fillets. Keep the Ø8.4 and Ø15 holes, which are fixed by M8 DIN 912.

suggested_change.detail: Unify internal radii to R3 or larger, so one Ø6 end mill does pocket and fillets

flags.title: No cost target or quantity in the blueprint
flags.evidence: blueprint.md frontmatter and §2-3 have no cost_target or quantity. Estimate assumes batch 10, 3-axis at EUR 60-90/h.
flags.recommendation: State the quantity and a unit-price target so that cost findings can be judged against them.

suggested_change.detail: Add quantity and cost_target to the blueprint

flags.title: Estimated unit cost about EUR 55-130 at batch 10 (rough)
flags.evidence: Assumptions: 6082 at EUR 4-8/kg, 1.0 kg stock gives EUR 4-8. Setups: 4 directions (+z, -z, -x, +y), so about 2 more handling steps than a 2-setup part (snapshot setup_directions). Machining about 40-75 min at EUR 60-90/h gives EUR 45-110, plus setup and programming amortised over 10 parts at about EUR 5-15. Anodising or other finishing is not included. Top drivers: (1) machining time across 4 setups, (2) the deep Ø3 side hole and 4 counterbores, (3) roughing away about 80% of the block.
flags.recommendation: Cheapest wins: cut setups to 2 (+z and -z) by moving or dropping the side hole, unify radii to R3, and check the stock choice.

suggested_change.detail: Estimate only; no model change implied
